nu-map/documentation / maintenance

Maintenance operational playbook

nu-map's course database requires manual refreshes — Northeastern provides no structured API. All data updates are initiated by you through the Dev Portal's Trigger tab; nothing runs automatically except data:patch:write (re-applied on every CI build). Every maintenance task is triggered by one of two things: the start of a new semester, or you found bad data.

Tool
Dev Portal — http://localhost:5173/northeastern/dev.html after npm run dev
Where to run
Trigger tab is local-only — HTTPS blocks its server calls. Run locally, push via Review & Push.
Deploy
Push to main → GitHub Actions → live in ~2 minutes. Patches re-applied automatically on every build.

Trigger A — start of semester (Jan / May / Sep)

flowchart TD START["Start of semester"] START --> CAT["Trigger tab → Course Catalog → ▷ Preview\nCheck for changed/new/missing courses"] CAT --> OK{"Changes look correct?"} OK -->|"Yes"| RUN["Course Catalog → ⚡ Run locally\nwrites catalog-courses.json + all-courses.json"] OK -->|"One field is wrong (catalog typo)"| PATCH["Skip that field — create a patch YAML instead\nnpm run data:patch:write to apply it"] OK -->|"100+ suspicious removals"| SKIP["Skip for now — verify on catalog.northeastern.edu first"] RUN & PATCH & SKIP --> NP["Trigger tab → NUPath Attributes → ⚡ Run locally\nfetches Tableau, updates nuPath fields"] NP --> AV["Trigger tab → Term Availability → ⚡ Run locally\nfetches Banner offering history → term-history.json"] AV --> PUSH["Review & Push → push to main\nCI deploys in ~2 min"]

Trigger B — you found bad data

SituationAction
One course, you know the fieldWrite a patch YAML → npm run data:patch:write → push. Patch survives all future scraper runs.
Unknown scope — want to see all differencesTrigger tab → Course Catalog → ▷ Preview
NUPath attributes specifically wrongTrigger tab → NUPath Attributes → ▷ Preview → ⚡ Run locally
Offering history (term-history.json) staleTrigger tab → Term Availability → ⚡ Run locally
Major requirements wrong or out of dateTrigger tab → Major Requirements → ⚡ Run locally (~45 min, rate-limited 600ms/req)

Patches — the permanent correction mechanism

Patches are the right tool when the catalog is wrong and our data is correct. Create a YAML file in data/northeastern/patches/, apply with npm run data:patch:write, commit — and every future CI build will re-apply it automatically. The catalog scraper can never silently overwrite a patched field.

# data/northeastern/patches/2025-09-01_fix-cs3700-credits.yaml
meta:
  date: "2025-09-01"
  reason: "Credits corrected per Fall 2025 catalog"
courses:
  update:
    - subject: CS
      number: "3700"
      fields:
        credits: 4
        nuPath: ["AD", "ND"]

Three action types: add (insert a course), update (change specific fields), remove (delete a course). Run npm run data:validate to check YAML schema before committing. Run npm run data:patch (no :write) for a dry-run preview.

CI pipeline — one push deploys everything

sequenceDiagram participant You participant GitHub participant CI as GitHub Actions participant Pages as gh-pages You->>GitHub: push to main GitHub->>CI: trigger deploy.yml CI->>CI: npm install CI->>CI: npm run data:patch:write Note over CI: re-applies all patches on top of
current catalog-courses.json CI->>CI: npm run build → dist/ CI->>Pages: deploy → live in ~2 min

Scripts reference

CommandWhat it doesWrites?
npm run devVite on :5173 + dev portal server on :3333No
npm run buildProduction build → dist/dist/
npm run data:scrapeDry-run: preview catalog changesNo
npm run data:scrape:writeScrape catalog + merge → catalog-courses.json, all-courses.jsonYes
npm run data:scrape:rotate:writeScrape one subject (round-robin) → catalog-courses.json. For incremental refreshes.Yes
npm run data:patchPreview patch application (dry-run)No
npm run data:patch:writeApply all patches. Idempotent. Runs automatically on every CI build.Yes
npm run data:validateValidate all patch YAML files for schema correctnessNo
npm run data:fetch:writeFetch base course records from husker.vercel.app → all-courses.jsonYes
npm run data:nupath:writeFetch NUPath attributes (Tableau + catalog fallback) → nupath-map.jsonYes
npm run data:nupath:apply:writeApply nupath-map.json to catalog-courses.jsonYes
npm run data:majors:writeScrape degree requirements → src/data/majors/ (~45 min)Yes
npm run data:majors:dryDry-run: first 5 programs only (sanity check)No
npm run testAll tests: rotate logic + CS2100 live checkNo
npm run dev:pwGenerate PBKDF2 password hash for dev portal authNo

End-of-semester checklist

  1. Dev Portal → Trigger tab → Course Catalog → ▷ Preview — review changes, then ⚡ Run locally.
  2. Trigger tab → NUPath Attributes → ⚡ Run locally.
  3. Trigger tab → Term Availability → ⚡ Run locally.
  4. Write patch YAMLs for any known catalog errors.
  5. If new catalog year: Major Requirements → ⚡ Run locally.
  6. npm run build → Dev Portal Preview tab — verify iPhone, iPad, Desktop.
  7. Trigger tab → Review & Push → push to main.

Setup

git clone https://github.com/nayugu/nu-map.git
cd nu-map
npm install
npm run dev    # Vite on :5173 + dev portal server on :3333

Node 18+. No environment variables needed for local development. The dev portal's password is a PBKDF2 hash embedded in dev.html — no server auth required.
